mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and corporate standing extracts of the Taiwan investor and each intermediate holding company in the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - Company Registration Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan cross-strait lane): Taiwan district-court notarization, Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification, ARATS/authorized municipal notary association authentication for mainland China. Do not apply a Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention Contracting Party.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Company Registration Information of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - Commercial and Industrial Registration Data Center
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan cross-strait lane): notarization by a Taiwan district-court notary, verification by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF), authentication by the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) / authorized provincial notary association; no Hague Apostille is attached or chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the CN WFOE, designating the legal representative, first directors and supervisors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investor; notarization by a Taiwan district-court notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan cross-strait lane): Taiwan notarization, SEF verification, ARATS/local notary association authentication for use in SAMR, tax and bank filings; the document is not eligible for Hague Apostille and must not be dual-authenticated.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Memorandum and Articles) of the Taiwan investor, including shareholding register and UBO declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor (certified copy) and Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan cross-strait lane): notarize the certified copy in Taiwan, submit through SEF for cross-strait verification, obtain ARATS-side authentication for the WFOE UBO filing; do not add a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the Taiwan investor's relationship bank confirming identity, good account conduct, source of funds and beneficial ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The Taiwan investor's licensed relationship bank (Taiwan financial institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Taiwan cross-strait lane): bank authorization and notarization, Taiwan notarization, SEF verification, ARATS-side authentication for mainland use; no Hague Apostille because Taiwan is not an Apostille Convention member.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding, screen all proposed UBOs, directors, legal representative, authorized signatories and senior managers against: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; EU and UK HMT consolidated sanctions lists; PRC Ministry of Public Security and PBOC adverse sanctions/blacklists; and Taiwan MOFA and central bank restricted trade and embargo lists. Determine PEP status (domestic, foreign and international-organization positions) through a structured questionnaire and negative-news search. Retest at opening of the WFOE bank account, annually, within 48 hours of any material ownership change, and before any dividend or cross-border platform payout. Any exact, alias or near-match hit requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds substantiation, senior-management sign-off and, where required, a timely SAMR/PBOC beneficial-owner filing update.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration and Pre-approval Online System (enterprise name self-service search and declaration portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be exclusively in standardized simplified Chinese characters; English names or Pinyin strings are not accepted in the SAMR registry. The name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + approved distinctive trade name + industry/operation characteristic + '有限公司' (limited-liability company). A foreign investor's Taiwan trade name may be transliterated into Chinese phonetically only if the transliteration does not conflict with protected trademarks or prior registered names. The industry segment must mirror the approved scope for ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210, e.g., information technology software development; terms requiring financial licenses such as bank, securities, fund, payment, clearing or settlement must not appear.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must obtain the written rejection notice stating the grounds under the 2021 Enterprise Name Registration Measures. Within 15 days, file an administrative appeal through the local SAMR online name module or in writing, addressing each rejection ground and providing the uniqueness analysis, trademark search results and the WFOE business-scope evidence. If the local Administration for Market Regulation upholds the rejection, file administrative reconsideration with the next-higher market regulation authority within 60 days of the written decision, or commence administrative litigation in the competent people's court within six months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial-mailbox-only address, or director-only registered address is impermissible for a Chinese WFOE. SAMR requires a legally obtained non-residential premises evidenced by a current lease or ownership certificate; the local tax bureau will reject taxpayer registration if there is no physical capacity to conduct business; and PRC banks mandate physical site visits, company nameplate inspection and management interviews for basic RMB account and SAFE capital-account registration. For the ISIC 6201 fintech-software business, a fully serviced co-working office with signed physical lease, visible nameplate, dedicated workstation and on-site staff is permissible; a remote-only virtual mailbox is not.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: lease agreement, property ownership certificate, landlord consent, company nameplate matching the registration, physical desks and staff, utility and internet bills in the WFOE name, accessible corporate records, and a compliant tax-invoice system. Quantified risk: 75% within the first 12 months for a mailbox-only address; 45% for a non-signposted co-working address; 15% for an actively staffed dedicated office. Unannounced physical inspections by municipal AMR or tax authorities are common during shell-company rectification campaigns and when invoice issuance, address filings and actual operations are inconsistent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended; applicable provisions include Articles 1, 2, 4, 6, 18, 40, 54, 98, 101, 108, 129, 137, 153-156, 161, 208, 387 and 393; together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4, 7, 8, 10 and 14, and the Regulations on Company Registration and Pre-Approval. The entity is formed as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company with permitted shareholding by non-resident persons.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company and Commerce One-Stop Services Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration together with the approved Articles of Incorporation, capital contribution schedule, first board resolution, proof of registered office, and capital verification report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for permitted software publishing and investment-tracking services under the Taiwan Companies Act. The subscribed capital stated in the Articles must be remitted to a Taiwanese bank account before the accountant's paid-in capital verification report is issued; funds may not be withdrawn or loaned to shareholders prior to registration. For foreign investment, the entire foreign-currency subscription may be remitted through an authorized foreign-exchange bank and verified. No blocked escrow account is required by the general incorporation regime; only the submitted capital must remain traceable and verified.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME], TAIWAN LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, CONVENED ON [DATE] AT [TIME] AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE AT [ADDRESS]. PRESENT: [DIRECTOR] AND, WHERE APPOINTED, [DIRECTOR]. THE CHAIRMAN DECLARES THAT A QUORUM IS PRESENT AND THAT THE FOLLOWING RESOLUTIONS ARE ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY. 1. CONSTITUTION AND LEGAL REGIME: RESOLVED that the Company be and hereby is constituted as a limited liability company under the Companies Act of Taiwan, with the name [COMPANY NAME] as approved by the competent authority, and the proposed Articles of Incorporation laid before this Board are approved and adopted in full as the governing instrument of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors be, and each of them is, authorized and directed to execute, acknowledge and file all instruments, declarations, applications and supplementary documents and to pay all registration fees necessary to obtain incorporation and good standing. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF CAPITAL: RESOLVED that the initial issued and paid-up capital of the Company be fixed at [CAPITAL AMOUNT] divided into one class of ordinary limited liability interests as set out in the capital contribution schedule. The subscriptions shown opposite each incorporator in the subscription schedule are hereby ratified, accepted and allotted, and the directors are directed to issue appropriate certificates or capital contribution records after full payment. RESOLVED FURTHER that the entire subscribed capital be deposited by the subscribers into the dedicated capital account of the Company at a licensed bank in Taiwan, and that no part of such capital be withdrawn, repaid, loaned or otherwise disbursed until the CPA capital verification report has been issued and the incorporation has been registered. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [ADDRESS] within Taiwan, that such address be maintained as the statutory registered office and be recorded in the Company Register, and that the directors be and they are hereby authorized to execute the lease, landlord consent or certificate of use and all ancillary documentation to perfect the registered office record. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the directors be and they are hereby authorized to open and maintain with such licensed bank or banks as they shall determine one or more accounts, including any foreign-currency account, and to execute all account-opening resolutions, corporate resolutions, mandates and indemnities required. RESOLVED FURTHER that [GENERAL MANAGER/DIRECTOR] and [CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER] be appointed as the sole or joint authorized bank signatories, with authority for any one such person to sign singly for all transactions and payments, and to adopt electronic banking platforms with such authentication protocols as the board may approve. 5. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [DIRECTOR NAME] be and hereby is appointed as the statutory Director of the Company and [SUPERVISOR NAME, IF ANY] be appointed statutory Supervisor, and [GENERAL MANAGER NAME] be appointed General Manager, each to serve in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the Companies Act. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Director, Supervisor and General Manager be severally authorized to effect the tax registration, uniform invoice registration, labor insurance and health insurance registration, and all ancillary registrations required for the lawful conduct of the business of personal wealth analytics and investment tracking software. 6. GOVERNANCE AND FILING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Chairperson and the General Manager, acting jointly or singly, be and they are hereby authorized to approve and affix the company seal, to execute the statutory declaration, to file the company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, and to engage legal counsel to respond to any query, objection or suspension notice, with full power to take all ancillary steps necessary to perfect the incorporation, governance and continuous good standing of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Name Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; name pre-check through the MOEA Company and Commerce One-Stop Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the foreign investor application electronically with the Investment Commission, MOEA before incorporation. The application must include a notarized certificate of incorporation of the foreign shareholder, current registered address and certificate of incumbency, audited financial statements, a legalized power of attorney, and a detailed business plan describing the financial portfolio tracking software, data protection measures, ownership structure and proposed capital remittance. The Commission will screen the project against the negative list for foreign investment; ISIC 6201 software publishing is generally a permitted activity. All foreign-language documents must be submitted with an accurate Chinese or English translation as required by the Commission. Upon approval, the Commission issues an Investment Approval Letter, which must accompany the company registration filing. Any change in ownership, capital, or business scope during review must be notified to the Commission before final approval.
required_dossiers: Investment application form
Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and notarized translation
Certificate of incumbency or register of directors
Audited financial statements of the foreign shareholder for the most recent year
Business plan and investment description
Power of attorney appointing Taiwan counsel or agent
Identity or passport copies of the Taiwan director and statutory officers
Proposed company name and purpose in Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, suspension, or deficiency notice, the applicant must file a supplementary explanation and all corrected documents within fourteen days of the notice. If the investment is denied, the applicant may request a pre-decision conference or file a reconsideration petition under the Administrative Appeal Act within thirty days after the written denial is served.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit, Foreign Exchange Verification and CPA Paid-in Capital Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized foreign-exchange bank in Taiwan and Taiwan-licensed Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital collection account with a Taiwanese bank that is authorized to handle foreign exchange transactions. Remit the subscribed capital from the foreign shareholder through an inward remittance routed to the designated account, ensuring the remittance reference identifies the subscriber and the purpose as capital contribution. The bank will issue the foreign exchange proceeds memorandum and inward remittance certificate. The appointed CPA reviews the bank statements, remittance receipts, foreign exchange documents and subscribed capital schedule, and then issues a paid-in capital verification report certifying that the full amount subscribed by each shareholder has been received in cash and remains available. This report must be based on current bank balance confirmation and must not be older than thirty days at the time of filing. The capital may not be used for any business purpose until the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Capital remittance application form
Inward remittance certificate from the bank
Foreign currency purchase or settlement memo
Bank account statement showing receipt of capital
Subscription schedule signed by each shareholder
CPA paid-in capital verification report
Foreign investment approval letter
Identity documents of subscribers and Taiwan company representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags the remittance under anti-money-laundering rules, the shareholder must submit a source-of-funds declaration, bank reference, and supporting transactional documents within ten business days. If the CPA refuses to certify the capital, the discrepancy must be corrected by the responsible shareholder and a superseding verification report submitted before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs One-Stop Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, Company and Commerce One-Stop Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the Investment Approval Letter and CPA capital verification report are available, submit the company registration application through the MOEA online one-stop portal. The proposed name must be cleared and the business scope stated in compliance with Taiwan Company Act registration rules. Upload the approved Articles of Incorporation, first board resolution, capital contribution schedule, registered office consent, director and supervisor appointment records, and identification documents. The portal will electronically calculate and collect the registration fee. Submit the original executed documents to the appointed filing agent for authentication with the company seal and bank signatory records. The Department of Commerce reviews for statutory compliance and issues the Company Registration Certificate. The company exists from the date of registration and must retain the registration certificate as conclusive evidence of its incorporation.
required_dossiers: Company registration application form
MOEA approved name pre-check
Articles of Incorporation
First board resolution
CPA capital verification report
Investment Approval Letter from Investment Commission
Registered office lease and landlord consent or title evidence
Passport or national identity card copies of directors and supervisor
Company seal card and specimen signatures
Power of attorney for the Taiwan filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the one-stop portal rejects or suspends the application, the filing agent must cure all stated deficiencies within fifteen days of the rejection notice. If the authority challenges the capital verification or investment approval, the applicant may submit supplementary explanations and legalization of supporting evidence. A merits appeal or administrative remedy is available under the Administrative Appeal Act within thirty days after the final refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Registration and E-Invoice Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; local branch with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within statutory time limits following company registration, the director or designee must appear before the local National Taxation Administration office to complete profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration and use of electronic uniform invoices. Submit the Company Registration Certificate, company seal card, corporate identification documents, registered office address proof, and bank account information. The tax authority will assign the tax identification number, issue the tax registration certificate, and confirm the company is placed on the uniform invoice registration system. The company must select an e-invoice service provider for issuing electronic receipts and sales invoices, designate an accounting and tax representative, and preserve statutory accounting records in New Taiwan Dollars and Chinese accordingly for future tax filing. Failure to complete tax registration can lead to penalties and delays in digital payment rails such as Stripe and Apple IAP merchant onboarding.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Company seal card and specimen of responsible person seal
Directors and supervisor identification documents
Proof of registered office address
Bank account deposit confirmation
Application for tax registration
Selection form for electronic uniform invoicing
Power of attorney for tax representative
Lease or ownership documentation for the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority rejects the registration or requests additional documentation, the company must resubmit within seven business days with the requested supporting evidence. If the rejection is based on incorrect tax classification or business address, the company may file a formal written correction and, if needed, an administrative appeal to the National Taxation Administration within thirty days of the adverse determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance, Statutory Records and Social/Labor Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Labor Bureau, National Health Insurance Administration, and MOEA Department of Commerce for beneficial ownership filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the board must ratify the first resolutions, adopt the company seal and bank signatories, and maintain a statutory shareholders register, board minutes book, and capital contribution ledger in accordance with the Companies Act. The company must file a beneficial owner declaration with the MOEA Department of Commerce within the prescribed period and keep the information updated. The company must next register as an employer with the local Labor Bureau for labor insurance and labor pension contributions, and with the National Health Insurance Administration for employee health insurance. In addition, the company must file the required labor safety and workplace health declarations for its office premises. This is a pure digital software activity and no industrial plant license is required; however, the office must comply with general fire safety requirements for evacuation route, extinguishers and alarm systems.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation and all resolutions
Shareholders register and capital contribution ledger
Beneficial owner disclosure form
Director and supervisor consent forms
Seal ledger and authorized signatory records
Labor insurance application and employee roster
Labor pension contribution application
National health insurance registration application
Office lease, floor plan and fire safety equipment checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the labor or health insurance authority rejects the registration because of incomplete wage records, the employer must resubmit within ten business days. If the beneficial ownership filing is queried by MOEA, the company must correct the report and provide source documents within fifteen days. For deficiencies found in a workplace fire safety inspection, the company must implement corrective measures and request a follow-up inspection within the period ordered by the local fire authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; ISIC 6201 software publishing is not a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity. For general office premises only, the local fire department and labor inspection agency have routine jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; no industrial operating permit or manufacturing license is required for this digital financial portfolio tracking software application.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; if a physical facility were ever established, the competent authority would be the Ministry of Environment of Taiwan (Environmental Protection Administration).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; no EIA registration, full EIA report, or environmental review is required for an office-based software business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the activity produces no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, hazardous waste storage, or air pollutant emissions. Standard office waste disposal and energy safety rules apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial and Civil Defense fire permits. As a pure software office, no Civil Defense operating fire permit is required, but the office must maintain basic fire safety equipment, unobstructed exits and extinguishers under local fire codes. Workplace health and safety compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act applies to general office operations and must be declared to the local labor inspection authority where required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; local STA tax service bureau at the WFOE's registered address; online operations through the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) and the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — incorporate the WFOE with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) and obtain the Business License of Enterprise Legal Person containing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Step 2 — within 30 days of business-license issuance, complete tax registration with the local STA via the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax); the USCC is the statutory TIN and VAT registration number, and no separate paper tax registration certificate is issued. Step 3 — elect VAT taxpayer status as general VAT taxpayer (mandatory when cumulative 12-month taxable turnover reaches CNY 5,000,000; voluntary below threshold) or small-scale taxpayer. Step 4 — activate the VAT invoice issuance quota and digital invoice seal through the Electronic Invoice Service Platform, complete the electronic filing/collection agreements, and bind the legal representative and accounting personnel to the e-Tax record. Step 5 — for a foreign non-resident investor/parent without a permanent establishment in China, no Chinese TIN is generally issued or required; China-sourced payments are covered by the WFOE's non-resident withholding registration and reporting. If the foreign party performs taxable activities in China through a branch or service operation, that branch/operation must separately register via the same e-Tax portal and obtain a USCC-based TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity-level income tax classification: China does not provide check-the-box, pass-through, or hybrid entity elections for a WFOE; a WFOE is automatically a resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income. The only relevant statutory election is the VAT status election between small-scale taxpayer and general taxpayer, and the taxpayer's choice to apply zero-rating or exemption to eligible cross-border services.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 of cumulative taxable turnover in any 12 consecutive months for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; no turnover threshold for basic tax registration, which is mandatory for all incorporated WFOEs from the date of establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory e-invoicing compliance framework. VAT invoices (ordinary and special) must be issued through the STA-controlled Electronic Invoice Service Platform as fully digitalized electronic invoices (digital invoices), bearing a unique invoice number, structured data file, and an anti-fraud digital seal/signature generated by the STA. Issuance and return data are transmitted to the tax authority in near-real time, with invoice quota and taxpayer profile managed online. For B2B and high-volume issuers, the WFOE is expected to use the platform API or e-Tax system for automated issuance, reporting, and reconciliation; paper invoices and traditional tax-control devices have been superseded for taxpayers registered in the digital-invoice system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero percent VAT (export zero-rating) or cross-border VAT exemption is available to a Chinese-resident VAT taxpayer for digital software/cloud services, including the personal wealth analytics and investment tracking application, when: (i) the recipient is a Taiwan/overseas enterprise or individual; (ii) the service is classified as software services or information technology services under the VAT reform rules; (iii) the service is wholly consumed outside mainland China; and (iv) the WFOE files the cross-border service declaration through the Electronic Tax Bureau and retains the statutory supporting documents. If the service is consumed in mainland China or the export conditions are not proven, domestic VAT applies (6% for modern services, or the applicable small-scale simplified rate).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (export customs declaration / bill of entry) and bill of lading or airway bill — required only for physical-goods exports; not applicable to the pure digital SaaS/App delivery in this scope.
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or the bank/PSP foreign-currency receipt and settlement voucher showing the Stripe or Apple IAP remitted proceeds.
Cross-border service contract, order form, or electronic subscription/terms of service identifying the Taiwan/overseas end customer and the service fee.

Service-consumption evidence: overseas IP logs, device or store-region data, user account data, usage analytics, or a customer declaration confirming the service is received and used outside mainland China.
Zero-rated or exempt fully digitalized electronic VAT invoice issued through the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform for the export transaction.
Export-service declaration / filing receipt generated by the Electronic Tax Bureau at the time of cross-border service reporting.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may audit export zero-rating/exemption claims by cross-checking e-invoice data, customs data (where applicable), FIRC/banking records, and overseas consumption evidence. Where zero-rating conditions are unverified or the claim is fraudulent, the uncharged VAT is clawed back retrospectively with late-payment interest from the original liability date; under

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, a vice-ministerial agency operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central banking authority for foreign exchange control and cross-border capital account administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a bifurcated foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations and SAFE administrative rules. Current account transactions are effectively convertible upon genuine verification by a designated foreign exchange bank, covering software subscription receipts, licensing fees, and ordinary operating disbursements. Capital account transactions remain controlled; a Taiwan-invested WFOE must obtain SAFE foreign exchange registration, open a dedicated capital account for FDI equity injection, and then convert registered capital into RMB for permitted operating purposes. There is no statutory mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds because SAFE abolished compulsory surrender in 2012; however, all current account foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated through designated banks with supporting contracts or invoices and reconciled through the trade-in-services monitoring system. Profit remittance to Taiwan shareholders is lawful after annual statutory audit, corporate income tax settlement, and submission of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and a board resolution to the settlement bank, with non-resident dividend withholding tax applied. The overall assessment is tight administrative control rather than full currency inconvertibility: the WFOE may conduct profitable RMB conversions if every transaction is backed by genuine commercial documentation and proper SAFE filing. Capital account liberalization is gradually expanding through pilot policies, but the bank compliance burden remains heavy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: SAFE imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender ratio; the statutory conversion ratio is 0% and the WFOE may retain foreign exchange or settle into RMB. For goods-trade exports, the 180-day collection rule applies from the customs declaration date under the Goods Trade Foreign Exchange Administration Measures. For software and services revenue, receipt must occur by contractual due date and be verified by the settlement bank. All proceeds must be repatriated to China unless an offshore retained account is approved; unrepatriated or overdue amounts trigger SAFE monitoring suspension and bank restrictions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and Core Operational Currency Account
Basic Deposit Account for Operational Clearing and Service Trade Settlement Account
Operational Settlement Account with Online FX Verification

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overseas digital fintech EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and Revolut Business are not licensed as Chinese payment institutions and are legally barred from opening local RMB settlement accounts or performing SAFE-declared current account conversions for a China-incorporated WFOE. They may only act as front-end collectors of foreign subscription receipts in limited scenarios and must downstream the funds into a licensed Chinese bank account for tax and SAFE reporting. The overall feasibility rating is Low for use as the primary treasury rail because such EMIs cannot provide compliant capital account registration, tax withholding documentation, or PBOC-recognized clearing. The WFOE should contractually use them solely for overseas collection and maintain Bank of China or ICBC as the authoritative clearing bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative or an expressly authorized senior officer holding a notarized power of attorney must attend a physical in-branch interview at the chosen tier-1 commercial bank. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard permissible route for newly incorporated Taiwan-invested WFOEs under current PBOC account-opening rules. Regional banks may accept a notarized video interview only for existing clients in exceptional extensions, but the conservative underwriting mandate for a cross-border fintech entity requires physical presence with original company chops, unified social credit code certificate, board resolutions, and passport identification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to establish source of funds for the Taiwan-origin capital injection into the WFOE capital account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Taiwan bank statements of the investing entity covering the latest 6 months, certified source-of-wealth documentation including tax filings and dividend certificates, the Taiwan parent board resolution approving the equity injection, and a notarized shareholder funding declaration linking every inward remittance to the subscribed registered capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) structure involving Taiwanese private holdings, nominee arrangements, or multi-layered trust vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified chain-of-ownership diagram from natural persons to the WFOE showing all shareholders above the 25% threshold, Taiwan company registration extracts, UBO passport copies, negative media and sanctions database screening reports from internationally accepted providers, and signed declarations of no nominee concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Financial portfolio tracking product perceived as unlicensed investment advisory, asset management, or brokerage activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written legal opinion from PRC counsel confirming the software does not provide securities advice, deposit taking, or client asset custody; the software copyright registration certificate; the end-user license agreement and privacy policy; a compliance commitment letter confirming that the WFOE never handles client funds; and a transactional flow diagram proving Stripe and Apple IAP route only data dashboards, not money management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border intellectual property transfer and data localization risk linked to Taiwan-licensed software engines and mainland user data.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The technology licensing agreement between the Taiwan parent and the WFOE, technical export control classification statement, data localization architecture for mainland users, and granular director/shareholder sanctions screening results with evidence of no adverse findings under Taiwanese or Chinese export control lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must route capital injection through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers using SAFE's foreign direct investment purpose code for equity capital contribution, with the beneficiary name exactly matching the WFOE's SAFE foreign exchange registration certificate. The receiving bank credits the funds into the capital account (foreign exchange capital account), then a PRC certified public accountant issues a capital verification report. RMB settlement is performed after confirming the WFOE business is not on the foreign investment negative list and after submitting the FDI report through the bank's national foreign exchange monitoring system. All remittances must carry the National Unified Social Credit Code and the FDI registration serial number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound software subscription refunds, licensing royalties to the Taiwan parent, and overseas marketing payments, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 after presenting a printed service trade foreign exchange declaration form and tax withholding proof. For physical goods or hardware bundles, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are acceptable under the same SAFE registration framework. Every outbound payment exceeding USD 50,000 requires underlying contract verification and tax payment certification; amounts above USD 500,000 trigger additional senior compliance review and may require submission of the original service contract to the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD forward contracts with a designated Chinese bank, covering registered capital conversion, service trade receipts, and projected licensing disbursements.
SAFE-approved cross-currency swaps for matching offshore Taiwan-dollar funding with RMB operational cashflows under real exposure limits.
FX swaps for temporary treasury liquidity positions between foreign currency capital account balances and RMB working capital.

Onshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for China-resident WFOEs; NDFs remain an offshore-only instrument and cannot be booked with a Chinese tier-1 commercial bank for hedging purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Meeting and Approval of Business Report, Financial Statements, and Profit Distribution Proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders General Meeting (internal body) acting as the company's supreme corporate organ; approval is then recorded in official minutes and used as the basis for external filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 of the year immediately following the calendar fiscal year end; equivalently, within six months after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the meeting is not convened by the statutory deadline, the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) may order the company's responsible person to convene within a specified period; persistent failure exposes the responsible person to administrative fines of NTD 10,000 to NTD 100,000 (approximately USD 320 to USD 3,200), and may delay or invalidate downstream statutory registrations, ultimately leading to removal of directors and administrative strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of the Approved Annual Financial Statements, Business Report, and Surplus Distribution or Deficit Absorption Proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Central Company Registration Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after approval by the shareholders meeting; for a calendar-year company this creates an effective hard deadline of July 15 (June 30 plus 15 days) unless an extension is formally granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission incurs an administrative fine of NTD 10,000 to NTD 50,000 (approximately USD 320 to USD 1,600) per infraction, with continued non-compliance triggering per-diem fines of NTD 2,000 to NTD 20,000 per day until rectification. An unrectified failure extending beyond one full fiscal cycle constitutes a non-operating corporate condition within the meaning of Company Act Article 10, empowering MOEA to dissolve and strike off the company administratively.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax-Reconciled Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year corporations, the filing window opens on April 1 and closes on May 31 immediately following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty accrues at 3% of the unpaid tax amount for every 15 days overdue, capped at 30% of the tax due; late payment interest accrues at 1.5% per annum on the tax shortfall. After a 7-day demand notice, the tax authority may impose a tax lien, freeze bank accounts, seize assets, and compulsorily collect. Failure to file for a full year allows the tax authority to make a unilateral assessment and bars the company from making lawful shareholder distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Annual Confirmation and Change Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) as AML registry authority; the Investment Commission receives cross-border ownership and transfer updates for foreign-invested companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership or significant control must be reported within 15 days of the triggering event; annual in-house confirmation is concurrently undertaken with the ordinary shareholders meeting and must be completed no later than June 30 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the UBO register is an AML administrative offence carrying fines of NTD 100,000 to NTD 500,000 (approximately USD 3,200 to USD 16,000); deliberate concealment of beneficial ownership may result in criminal prosecution under the Money Laundering Control Act, and repeated non-compliance supports MOEA administrative dissolution and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Company Act and related MOEA and Financial Supervisory Commission rules, a mandatory independent certified CPA audit is triggered when any of the following quantitative or qualitative criteria are satisfied: (1) paid-in capital exceeds NTD 30 million (approximately USD 1 million); (2) the company is a public company or a company otherwise listed with securities authorities; (3) the company is a bank, financial holding company, insurer, securities dealer, or other financial institution regulated by the FSC; (4) annual revenue exceeds NTD 100 million (approximately USD 3.2 million) and the company is designated by the central authority; or (5) the competent authority or the Investment Commission specifically requires an audited balance sheet and income statement for foreign-invested or cross-border registration purposes. The audit must be performed by an independent CPA who may not serve concurrently as the company's bookkeeper or internal accountant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS), which comprises the International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed and issued by the Financial Supervisory Commission. Non-public small and medium-size companies may elect to apply the Business Entity Accounting Standards (Taiwan EAS) adopted under the Company Act, or they may voluntarily adopt TIFRS on a consistent basis. The CPA's examination is conducted in accordance with Taiwan Statements of Auditing Standards (TW SAS), and for foreign-invested enterprises the annual financial statements may be subject to supplementary reconciliation and attestation requirements imposed by the Investment Commission.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company is required to maintain a current and complete register of beneficial owners and significant controllers at its registered office. Under the Money Laundering Control Act and Company Act beneficial ownership disclosure rules, any transfer of shares, change in voting control, or modification of the ownership chain must be lodged with MOEA and, where applicable, with the Investment Commission, within 15 days of the event. Although Taiwan does not impose a standalone annual UBO return, the company must continuously update the register and, as a matter of statutory good governance, confirm the accuracy of the UBO list at the annual shareholders meeting no later than June 30 of each year. A failure to make a timely report after a shareholding transfer nullifies the legal reliance that the company can place on shareholder approval and exposes the responsible person to the AML penalties described below.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 to 2,500 per annum for a licensed Taipei-based corporate service provision, including a physical registered office address, company secretarial coordination, correspondence handling, and registry monitoring.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 to 9,000 per annum for a low-risk fintech SaaS entity with straightforward financial statements and no statutory license; the fee range assumes a single-entity local GAAP audit, with higher pricing if consolidated TIFRS reporting or cross-border reconciliation is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible High and New Technology Enterprise may reduce the statutory rate to 15%; qualified software and fintech enterprises may access a two-year exemption followed by three-year 50% reduction; additional deduction of 100% for qualifying R&D expenses; small low-profit enterprises may enjoy an effective 5% rate on taxable income up to RMB 3 million under current preferential rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A) and supporting schedules; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return is due within 5 months of the fiscal year-end (normally 31 May); quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue, other operating revenue, and non-operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income because the China-incorporated WFOE is a Chinese tax resident. Include revenue from financial portfolio tracking subscriptions and cloud analytics. Revenue from the Taiwan parent or Taiwanese clients must be recognized at arm's length and supported by contracts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of main operations and other operating costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs evidenced by proper invoices and service agreements. Payments to the Taiwan parent for cloud platform, data licensing, or technology support must be substantiated as actual services; otherwise they are disallowed or recharacterized by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges other than Corporate Income Tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only indirect tax surcharges such as urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and stamp duty. Corporate Income Tax itself is not deductible.

Include deductible R&D expenses eligible for super deductions. Management fees paid to the Taiwan parent are non-deductible unless the payer can prove genuine services were rendered and that the pricing is at arm's length. Royalty payments must satisfy beneficial ownership and economic substance tests.

Apply the thin capitalization rule: interest paid on related-party debt exceeding the prescribed debt-to-equity ratio (2:1 for non-financial enterprises) is non-deductible. Interest paid to the Taiwan parent must also satisfy the arm's length principle and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction disclosure and cross-border non-resident transaction schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all transactions with the Taiwan parent and related parties, including technology fees, management fees, interest, loans, and share transfers. Failure to disclose triggers audit risk and may invalidate treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, loss carryforward, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 5-year ordinary carryforward limit; a 10-year limit may apply to qualifying high-new technology enterprises. Foreign tax credits are available only with proper foreign tax evidence and are subject to the China worldwide income regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate Income Tax payable after preferential rates and withholding obligations on outbound distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When declaring a dividend to the Taiwan parent, separately report the non-resident dividend withholding tax. The WFOE is the statutory withholding agent and must withhold and remit tax at the applicable source rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may attract a penalty under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Administration Law of up to RMB 2,000, or RMB 10,000 in serious cases; late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Under- or non-declaration may trigger Article 63 evasion penalties of between 50% and 500% of the underpaid tax; criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 may lead to imprisonment up to three years for ordinary evasion and up to seven years for serious evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise, including a Taiwan parent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction tax authority, complete the treaty benefit application, and prove it is the beneficial owner of the dividend. The Chinese payer must file the withholding reduction application through the electronic tax portal before the distribution; the tax authority may deny relief if the recipient lacks economic substance, employees, premises, or real control over the income. In the Taiwan context, there is no full PRC-Taiwan comprehensive double tax treaty; the limited Cross-Strait tax agreement may apply only if the Taiwan beneficial owner satisfies strict residency and substance conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax is 10% on gross royalty and interest paid to a non-resident. Reduced treaty rates may be available under applicable agreements, but for Taiwan the statutory 10% is the normal source-country rate absent successful relief under the limited Cross-Strait agreement. Interest and royalty relief requires a TRC, beneficial ownership declaration, arm's length pricing, and demonstrable core income-generating activities in the recipient's jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million for annual related-party tangible property transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible or financial asset transfers; RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions. Master File is generally required when the group's consolidated annual revenue reaches RMB 2.5 billion and related-party transaction thresholds are met.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies a substance-over-form doctrine under its General Anti-Avoidance Rule and the Enterprise Income Tax Law. Although there is no offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations filing in China, tax authorities will examine the Core Income-Generating Activities, employees, premises, risk exposure, and decision-making functions of both the Chinese WFOE and the Taiwan shareholder before granting treaty benefits or allowing related-party deductions. A shell entity with no real business substance will be disregarded and income will be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the WFOE as a letter-box company with no employees, no physical office, no local decision-making, and no management substance while booking financial analytics income and capital gains in China or routing treaty benefits through Taiwan purely to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and Implementation Regulations authorize the tax authority to recharacterize the transaction under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule; the tax authority may impose special tax adjustment within 10 years, add interest, and impose late payment surcharges and penalties up to 50% of the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under PRC Company Law Article 20, a court may pierce the corporate veil if the shareholder or director abuses the limited liability structure to harm creditors or the tax authority; directors may be ordered to restore assets personally, subjected to asset freezes, travel bans and tax blacklisting, and in serious cases may face criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 with imprisonment up to seven years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making excessive management fees, royalty payments, or intercompany interest payments to the Taiwan parent without functional analysis, benchmark studies, or arm's length documentation, causing the Chinese WFOE to report chronic losses or artificially low profit while value is shifted outside China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 41 and 46, together with SAT Bulletin 2016 No. 42, allow a transfer pricing audit, upward adjustment of taxable income, disallowance of excessive deductions, charging of interest on the adjustment, a daily late payment surcharge, and an evasion penalty under Article 63 of the Tax Administration Law of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve false transfer pricing documentation or knowingly cause the company to underpay tax may be jointly and severally liable for the tax debt; the public security authorities may place them on exit control lists, freeze personal assets, and impose criminal liability for false tax filings, with imprisonment terms of up to seven years under Criminal Law Article 201.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold on Outbound Dividends and Abusive Treaty Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to the Taiwan parent without withholding 10% non-resident dividend tax, or claiming treaty relief without a valid Tax Residency Certificate and without proving beneficial ownership, or structuring the distribution through a conduit entity with no economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Tax Administration Law Article 69, a withholding agent that fails to withhold and remit tax is liable to a penalty of between 50% and 300% of the amount that should have been withheld; the tax authority may also collect the underpaid tax from the withholding agent and impose daily late payment surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Practicing directors who caused the company to breach withholding obligations may be personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties; the tax authority may blacklist the company and its responsible directors, impose travel bans, restrict exit from China, and pursue criminal investigation for intentional tax non-remittance, leading to imprisonment and confiscation of personal assets.
